_metadata.title: Distractor Quality Review — Absolutist / Low-Quality Signals
_metadata.scope: All 5 packs (2,500 questions). Choices and ExplanationWrong fields scanned for absolutist language patterns.
corrections_applied: Pack B "all of the above" items (P1B-E-087, P1B-E-150, P1B-F-100): reclassified KEEP_AS_IS — these are correct answers, not distractors
P1-E-058 EW C: reclassified KEEP_AS_IS — false positive ("without exception reports" = COSO term, not absolutist)
Pack A items (P1-A-008, P1-B-074, P1-D-004): DL-016 metadata-content mismatch may affect QID association
Pack C CC-021 through CC-027: confirmed DL-012 clone group with absolutist distractor text
_metadata.note: All proposed distractor rewrites are read-only staging. No pack files have been modified. Actual edits require a separate "apply approved changes" session after SME review.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Zephyr reduced inventory quantities below older LIFO layers during a period of rising costs. Which response is most appr
candidates.original_distractor: Assume LIFO liquidation always decreases income
candidates.proposed_distractor: Consider whether the decline in replacement cost is temporary
candidates.rationale: Replace absolute claim with a more nuanced alternative that a rushed candidate might select. Original: "Assume LIFO liquidation always decreases income."

candidates.stem_excerpt: Oakhaven uses participative budgeting, allowing department managers to set their own targets. Beyond budgetary slack, wh
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees higher employee morale in every case
candidates.proposed_distractor: It consistently leads to higher employee satisfaction with the budget process
candidates.rationale: Replace "guarantees higher employee morale in every case" with a softened version that still acknowledges the participative budgeting benefit without absolutist language.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Yukon has partially completed units at period-end. Which response is most appropriate?
candidates.original_distractor: Count partially completed units as zero in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: Exclude partially completed units from the equivalent unit calculation
candidates.rationale: Replace "Count partially completed units as zero in all cases" with a more technically accurate distractor that a candidate confusing process costing with job costing might select.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Vesper's divisions negotiate a transfer price between the market price and the selling division's variable cost. What is
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees goal congruence in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: It eliminates all transfer pricing disputes between divisions
candidates.rationale: More nuanced: negotiated pricing may reduce but cannot eliminate all disputes. This is plausible to a candidate who overestimates negotiation benefits.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Westbrook's divisions negotiate a transfer price between the market price and the selling division's variable cost. What
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees goal congruence in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: It automatically aligns divisional goals with corporate objectives
candidates.rationale: More realistic: negotiated transfer prices can help align goals but do not do so automatically. Requires ongoing negotiation and may break down under capacity constraints.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Yarrow's divisions negotiate a transfer price between the market price and the selling division's variable cost. What is
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees goal congruence in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: It eliminates the need for top management intervention in transfer pricing
candidates.rationale: Plausible to a candidate who confuses negotiation with autonomy. Top management may still need to intervene when divisions cannot agree.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Zenith Bay's divisions negotiate a transfer price between the market price and the selling division's variable cost. Wha
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees goal congruence in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: It automatically results in the same transfer price as market-based pricing
candidates.rationale: Plausible to a candidate who doesn't recognize that negotiated prices can deviate from market when cost structures differ.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Ashgrove's divisions negotiate a transfer price between the market price and the selling division's variable cost. What
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees goal congruence in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: It prevents all suboptimization by selling divisions
candidates.rationale: More realistic: negotiation helps but cannot prevent all suboptimization, especially when external market prices fluctuate.

candidates.stem_excerpt: Birchwood's divisions negotiate a transfer price between the market price and the selling division's variable cost. What
candidates.original_distractor: It guarantees goal congruence in all cases
candidates.proposed_distractor: It makes the transfer price irrelevant to divisional performance evaluation
candidates.rationale: Plausible to a candidate who mistakenly thinks negotiation makes the price neutral to both divisions.
